summary.text: Daughter whom Alcmaeon begot on Manto daughter of Tiresias in the Euripidean variant of his madness — not the Erinys Tisiphone of the Erinyes (`tisiphone-erinyes`); fostered at Corinth by Creon, sold as a slave by the queen, and unknowingly bought back by her father before he recovered his son Amphilochus.

story.text: Apollodorus reports a Euripidean strand beside the canonical brother of Alcmaeon born to Eriphyle: in madness Alcmaeon begot Amphilochus and Tisiphone on Manto, daughter of the Theban seer Tiresias, and brought the infants to Creon king of Corinth to be reared.

Because of her extraordinary beauty, Creon's wife feared the king might marry the girl and sold her as a slave. Alcmaeon later bought her as a handmaid without knowing she was his daughter; coming to Corinth to recover his children, he learned the truth and took back both daughter and son.

The name is shared with the Erinys Tisiphone whom Hesiod and Apollodorus name among the Furies born from Uranus' blood — a wholly different figure, kept under the suffixed id `tisiphone-erinyes` in the atlas homonym map.
